newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gunman gives up after two injured in Swiss church.
newsitem.headline: Gunman gives up after two injured in Swiss church.

text.p: A gunman who shot and wounded two people in a Geneva church surrendered to Swiss police early on Sunday after holing up for six hours in the building.
"He has surrendered. He has been arrested," said a police spokesman.
The gunman opened fire in the Notre Dame Roman Catholic church shortly after evening mass ended at 7.30 p.m. (1830 GMT), wounding a priest and a sexton in the legs.
Armed police surrounded the city centre church and brought in psychologists to try to calm the man down.
The gunman, whose motives remained unclear, demanded to see the city's police chiefs.
Police said he made a series of calls with a mobile phone. The man was believed to be a lawyer and former Swiss army officer.
The two wounded were removed from the church together with other worshippers. They were taken to hospital where police said their wounds were not serious.
During the siege, policemen with sniffer dogs moved around the edge of the church, near Geneva's main railway station and the four-star Hotel Cornavin, apparently searching for explosives.
Outside the church, about a dozen police officers wearing flak jackets, black masks and helmets trained their guns on the building.
Geneva residents were shocked by the attack, the first they could remember in their normally tranquil city.
"There's a gunman down the road, haven't you heard?," an elderly Swiss lady in a black coat shouted at passers-by in a nearby street.
A young police officer told a group of cinema-goers asking what had happened: "There's been shooting. Someone has been shooting."
Switzerland has compulsory military service for men and every able-bodied Swiss male has an assault weapon at home. Switzerland has a 400,000-strong militia army.
